newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Africa -- engine of world growth in 21st century?.
newsitem.headline: Africa -- engine of world growth in 21st century?.

text.p: Africa, currently the world's poorest continent, has the potential to become the engine of world economic growth in the second quarter of the 21st century, Ivory Coast's prime minister said on Monday.

Daniel Kablan Duncan opened a two-day ministerial meeting preparing for Wednesday's launch of the Alliance for Africa's Industrialisation, saying Africa should aim to achieve strong and lasting growth from 2026.
"The growth of the African economy by its vitality could be during this period the main engine of world growth as Asia is at present," he added.

The Alliance is being set up under the auspices of the U.N. Industrial Development Organisation (UNIDO). It aims to promote industrialisation in Africa by focusing initially on links between agriculture and industry.
Duncan said that Africa's growth rate between 1990 and 1993 was 1.4 percent compared to 8.83 percent for Asia.
He said that Ivory Coast, which portrays itself as the Elephant of Africa, aimed to join the ranks of newly industrialised nations within a generation -- "in 25-30 years".

UNIDO director general, Mauricio De Maria Y Campos, said the Alliance offered Africa the opportunity to end its marginalisation in the world economy. "This image of Africa as a lost continent must be changed," he said.
A meeting of heads of state in Ivory Coast's commercial capital Abidjan on Wednesday will launch the Alliance. It was not immediately clear how many presidents would be present.
